pageCache.pageTitle: Our Christian Values - St Margarets CEVA Primary School
pageCache.text:
I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me.
Philippians 4:13 states,
“I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me.” This verse emphasises the belief that believers can overcome any challenge or difficulty in life by relying on Christ’s strength.
Love: We want St Margaret’s pupils to develop a love of learning that will grow as they travel through their educational career and beyond. We work together to nurture an inquisitive love of learning by including many exciting learning opportunities.
Honesty: St Margaret’s pupils are encouraged to be honest and they are given a platform to do so. Discussions in our curriculum about British Values, diversity and what is happening in the world today, encourages honest speaking. Pupils at St Margaret’s learn that their views are valued and welcome.
Courage: St Margaret’s pupils are able to achieve because they believe in themselves and in each other. This takes courage, and when our pupils face new challenges they embrace each one and give them their best shot!
Friendship: Friendship is an important part of our curriculum at St Margaret’s. Pupils will support each other through their learning and encourage each other to try new things, step outside their comfort zone or learn from making mistakes. Friendship encourages a safe environment in which to learn.
Respect: Everybody at St Margaret’s is unique and everybody is welcome here. Recent converts to the ‘No Outsiders programme’ has helped support this view and has encouraged many debates. Just as each person is unique so is each person’s way of learning. Teachers and children work hard to make sure that all learning styles are catered for and that everyone is able to achieve to the best of their ability.
Trust: In order to deliver a progressive, forward thinking, exciting curriculum all stakeholders at St Margaret’s need to trust each other. Pupils trust that the education they receive is created specifically for them; teachers need to trust that pupils will embrace the curriculum and apply themselves fully; parents and Governors need to trust that the pupils are at the centre of decisions made about the curriculum. All stakeholders have confidence in the curriculum that is being delivered.
At St Margaret’s our curriculum is designed to ensure our young people leave us with high aspirations; they will know how to make a positive contribution to their own and the wider community. We aim to challenge all learners through rich curricular and extra-curricular opportunities. This will help our pupils to become resilient learners who are not afraid to take risks, solve problems or be creative. We strive to ensure that our learning environment is positive, happy and stimulating for pupils and other stakeholders. Children will reach at least age related expectations in reading, writing and maths. Children with SEND will also reach their full potential. Our pupils are learning for life and our role is to offer them a curriculum that will support this.
Our school has 6 Christian Values spread out over two years. We link these values within all of our school life including our Collective Worship sessions. Children are awarded leaves during our Celebration Collective Worships for demonstrating these values.
In 2026-2027 our values are:Autumn: CourageSpring: LoveSummer: Honesty
In 2025 – 2026 our values are:Autumn: FriendshipSpring: RespectSummer: Trust

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome - St Margarets CEVA Primary School
pageCache.text:
St Margaret’s CEVA School
We can do all things through Christ who strengthens us – Philippians 4:13
I am delighted that you have chosen to find out more about us and hope you find our website informative.I am incredibly proud to be the Head Teacher of St Margaret’s CEVA Primary School. Since arriving here in September 2019 I have had the pleasure of working with a dedicated team that work tirelessly to ensure that our children receive the best education that will support and provide a solid foundation for their choices later in life. We focus on our School Core Values of, Love, honesty, courage, respect, friendship, trust.
One of the most often heard saying about St Margaret’s is that it is a ‘family school’ and I must say that I totally agree. We are a small village primary school set in the beautiful village of Tintinhull, just outside Yeovil. We have 4 classes and a purpose built pre-school/nursery on site. Children join us from age 2 and stay until the end of Year 6. Having the pre-school on site ensures that a smooth transition into school is supported. The children in preschool know the teachers and staff before they start at the school, as we work together with them and they are included in lots of school activities. Head over to their webpage to see what they get up too! (Discoverers).
We have a close connection with the local community and we regularly share school news in the local village magazine. We work with other agencies to make a difference in the community and we take pride in being able to support local events. It is important to us that our children recognise that they have responsibility to care and support others. We do this in many ways including: connections with our local care home, ST Margaret’s Church, working with the local rotary group and joining in with village events to name just a few!
We strive to ensure that our children experience an interesting, thought provoking, safe learning environment where they are able to develop and grow into confident learners. Parents, Governors, volunteers and the PFA all play a part of this and we would love you to come and join us.
If you require further information or wish to arrange a visit to our school, please do not hesitate to contact Mrs Morgan or Mrs Facey on 01935 822686 or office@stmargaretsceva.com
Important Safeguarding Information:
What if I’m worried about my child or another child?If you’re finding it hard at home with your child and are struggling to cope, call Family Lives for free, confidential advice on 0808 800 2222.
If you’re worried about the safety of another child in our community, call the NSPCC on 0808 800 5000. Or call the police on 999 if you think a child is in immediate danger.

pageCache.pageTitle: Wraparound Care - St Margarets CEVA Primary School
pageCache.text:
We operate a Breakfast Club opening from 8:00am until morning registration. Children are provided with a range of cereals to choose from as well as toast with a choice of condiments. Water, milk, apple or orange juice are available as drinks. The cost is £4.50 including breakfast. Bookings can be made in advance via Parentmail with payment required at the time of booking.
Stay & Play after school opens from the end of the school day and closes at 5:00pm. Children are given a small snack and a drink. There are a choice of finish times – 4:30pm or 5:00pm. The cost is £4.50 for the 4:30pm finish and £6.50 for the 5:00pm finish. Bookings can be made in advance via Parentmail with payment required at the time of booking.

How our curriculum works
Our curriculum aims to develop confident, resilient learners who value different perspectives. Read about our implementation and the wider national curriculum below.
Our curriculum implementation (PDF)
The national curriculum
Our curriculum vision
At St Margaret’s, our curriculum is crafted to spark creativity, nurture personal growth, and equip children with the skills and mindset needed for life beyond the classroom. We are committed to delivering rich, memorable learning experiences that foster strong relationships, emotional resilience, and a deep appreciation for mental health and wellbeing.
Our approach is rooted in a well-structured, knowledge-rich curriculum that aims to inspire every learner and support high levels of achievement. We encourage pupils to develop expertise across a range of subjects—from history and geography to science and the arts. Through our themed terms—Discover, Explore, and Create, children are invited to fully engage in their learning journey and embrace curiosity and adventure.
Building Knowledge with Purpose
A successful curriculum depends on secure, cumulative knowledge that grows year by year. Our teaching teams collaborate to plan subject content from EYFS through to Year 6, ensuring continuity and progression are central to every child’s experience.
We are proud to be working with the Boolean Maths Hub to embed a mastery approach in Numeracy, and our Literacy leads are partnering with the Cornerstone Hub to strengthen reading and writing outcomes. The introduction of the Little Wandle phonics programme ensures our teaching aligns with national guidance and supports early reading development effectively.
To explore how our curriculum is implemented across different areas, please download the document below:
Curriculum Impact
Every aspiration is valued – whether a child dreams of becoming a scientist or a dancer, their goals are recognised and respected equally.
Children experience a vibrant, broad, and engaging curriculum that motivates and inspires.
Pupils progress through each stage of their education as confident, resilient problem-solvers, ready and eager for what comes next.
Our learners grow into well-rounded individuals who appreciate diversity, understand global perspectives, and celebrate differences.
Children set high standards for themselves and strive to meet them.

pageCache.pageTitle: SEND - St Margarets CEVA Primary School
pageCache.text:
Our SENDCo is Mrs Melanie Leeson.She is in school every Wednesday and can be contacted via the school office:Telephone: 01935 822686 or email: office@stmargaretsceva.com
At St. Margaret’s, we are a fully inclusive school. Our aim is for all pupils to achieve their potential personally, socially, emotionally and academically in all areas of the curriculum. We are small village school that has recently incorporated a brand-new purpose-built therapy suite that includes a disabled toilet, accessible shower and space for a changing bed. The building is on one level and can be accessed via ramps at the front and rear of the school. Close to the playground we also have a Learning Lodge that can be utilised as a classroom or as an ELSA room. Our staff are all very nurturing and knowledgeable with a wealth of experience supporting children in all aspects of Special Educational Needs.All Somerset maintained schools have a similar approach to meeting the needs of pupils with special educational needs and are supported by the Local Authority to ensure that all pupils, regardless of their specific needs, make the best possible progress in school. We are committed to supporting pupils with needs in all four broad areas of the SEND Code of Practice: Cognition and Learning, Communication and Interaction, Social and emotional mental health and Sensory and/or Physical needs.The SEND information report highlights how we identify, support and assess pupils with SEND to ensure they make progress academically, socially and emotionally.
​Somerset SEND Local OfferDetails on how the local authority supports pupils with Special Educational Needs or Disabilities can be found in Somerset’s local offer which can be accessed via this link: www.somerset.gov.uk/local-offer
Somerset Parent Carer Forum can be accessed via this link: https://somersetparentcarerforum.org.uk/
Somerset SENDIAS- SEN and Disability, Information and Advice Service (formerly Somerset Parent Partnership) can be accessed via this link: https://somersetsend.org.uk/
For more information, please read the policies, audits and documents below
